summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (for later question-answering; use these instead of source)

## Notes on the text's form
- Three separate works, each headed "BOOK n of 3". Book 1 = *The Yellow House; Master of Men* (E. Phillips Oppenheim). Book 2 = *Emmanuel Appadocca; or, Blighted Life* (Maxwell Philip, 2 vols, 1854). Book 3 = *The Great White Army* (Max Pemberton, 1916).
- Book 1 also includes a Gutenberg transcriber's note listing corrections (e.g., "her"→"hear", "pefect"→"perfect", "Ig"→"If", "I"→"It", "haid"→"said", "Berdentein"→"Berdenstein", "enchanged"→"exchanged", "nonense"→"nonsense", "whereever"→"wherever").
- Book 2 has a note: "There are two CHAPTER XXIIIs" (vol. 2 has two chapters numbered XXIII).

---

## BOOK 1: THE YELLOW HOUSE; MASTER OF MEN (Oppenheim)
Volume One; NY: P.F. Collier & Son, 1908/1912. Narrator: Kate Ffolliot, daughter of Rev. Horace Ffolliot, curate-in-charge at a Northshire village (Dorset-like; Vicarage, Deville Court nearby). Sister: Alice (plain, dutiful, conventional, "literal"). Servant: Mary (maid), Morris (servant/gardener), Bekky? (no, that's Book 2). Kate was raised abroad (school at Berlin, Heidelberg; took good degree at Heidelberg); came home ~8–9 months before.

**Ch I – The Yellow House.** Callers: Countess of Sysington (from Sysington Hall, 12 miles; two anaemic daughters), Holgates of Holgate Brand, Lady Amy Naselton (of Naselton Hall; middle-aged, bright, matchmaker, Kate's sponsor; husband mentioned; son Fred). Father claims relation to Warwickshire Ffolliots (with "second f"). Only two not calling: Mr. Bruce Deville of Deville Court (Lady Naselton's godson; "lord of the Manor of a dozen parishes"; ugly, slouches, brutal temper, ex-world wanderer 12 yrs, spent fortune on singer Marie Leparte; returned ~4 yrs ago, living in one room with old servant; "ruined") and the woman in the "Yellow House" (a "shanty" through the plantation, who followed Deville down and was furnished from the Court). Lady N. says Deville "failure". Father faints/reacts when Deville's name said: "Mr. Bruce Deville… somewhat an uncommon name"; father warns girls to avoid him.

**Ch II – On the Moor.** Alice reads to old woman; Kate restless. At gate, Kate overhears Deville (tall, broad, beard, long hair, rent shooting coat, beagles, whip: "Get over, Madam! Get over, Marvel!") and a woman (Adelaide Fortress, unseen) talking of "new vicar… with a daughter"; Deville: "a pale-faced, black-haired chit." Father, returning, collapses in the garden; after revival says "It was her voice… through the shadows!"

**Ch III – Mr. Bruce Deville.** Father's first sermon successful; Lady N. urges him for cathedral. Deville's beagle (Lawless) with broken leg; Kate binds it. Deville: traps set by tenant Harrison. Kate introduces herself ("Miss Ffolliot… the pale-faced chit"). Father and Deville meet hostilely: Deville: "I need no introduction… I can offer you no welcome." Father: "I desire no welcome from you." Father, shaken: "That man was closely… associated with the most unhappy chapter of my life." Deville: "until the end, and God grant that it may not be long."

**Ch IV – Our Mysterious Neighbors.** Storm; Kate takes shelter at Yellow House; meets Adelaide Fortress (dark eyes, 35–40, thin, grey-touched brown hair, Socialist, electioneered for Mr. Densham at Belchester, writes for newspapers, Dresden cups, Penates). Deville arrives in dress through window; Marcia (Fortress's first name — father calls her "Marcia"). Father storms in: "That is precisely what my daughter will do, madam!" Father and Marcia's eyes meet; "Marcia!" "You had better go."

**Ch V – A South American Letter.** Father receives letter from South America (square envelope, fine writing, "London about fifteenth") and goes to London (Annesly Junction 3.30; St. Pancras). Says he'll return Friday. Kate finds Deville's dropped envelope has same handwriting. Father had been at Belchester; Colonel Dacre complained to Bishop of his London trips.

**Ch VI – The Millionaire.** Lady N. (note "Thursday") introduces Mr. Berdenstein (sallow, Jewish-type, showy teeth, millionaire, from Rio, South America; Fred Naselton's benefactor; had a sister in Paris; "Adelaide Fortress"—he's obsessed with her; "I am going to regain her or die!"). Berdenstein: "Stephen" (given later). He begs Kate not to tell Fortress.

**Ch VII – A Fruitless Appeal.** Father doesn't return Saturday. Kate goes to Fortress and Deville; she accuses them, names Berdenstein at Naselton Hall. Fortress: "Child… I believe your father is well." Father returns on foot, with revolver (small, shining); goes home, looks ghastly.

**Ch VIII – The Coming of Mr. Berdenstein.** Sunday. Father ill (bandage/wound later). Bishop of Exchester visiting Lady N.; father to preach. Kate walks with father to Bromilow Downs; they meet Berdenstein (real name Stephen Berdenstein) on road; father sends Kate off ("call on Mr. Charlsworth"); father takes Berdenstein toward Deville Court.

**Ch IX – A Terrible Interruption.** Evensong; father preaches "The wages of sin is death"; Berdenstein, bloody, staggers into church, cries "Judas! you, Judas! Oh! my God!" and collapses; dies; inquest says murder in plantation between downs and Yellow House. Bishop: "God grant that he may have found [sanctuary]."

**Ch X – Canon of Belchester.** Kate ill ~a week; Deville sends roses/violets. Father to be made Canon. Inquest: no witness; father not called. Father visits; Kate asks; he refuses to explain ("It was the will of God").

**Ch XI – The Gathering of the Cloud.** Father admits meeting Berdenstein, that it's secret; "I cannot offer you my whole confidence"; they're moving to Eastminster; Kate promises silence then says she'll leave.

**Ch XII – Mr. Berdenstein's Sister.** Olive Berdenstein (sister; short, dark, thin, plain, rich dresser, diamonds) comes; seeks "Philip Maltabar" (father's alias; enemy of Stephen). Father refuses to see her ("No! no! I cannot see her").

**Ch XIII – For Vengeance.** Father hides. Kate meets Deville; he says Adelaide's idea of roses. Deville: "Don't say anything rude…"

**Ch XIV – Adelaide Fortress's Guest.** Father wounded (bandage soaked with blood, from Berdenstein's knife, "cowardly attack… the night before I returned"). Kate meets Deville at lane; Deville asks where father is; he tells Kate father's better out of the way. At Yellow House: Olive Berdenstein with Adelaide, reunion with Deville ("At last!"—Olive recognizes him from Baeren/Switzerland rescue).

**Ch XV – The Likeness of Philip Maltabar.** Olive finds photo in Adelaide's cabinet secret compartment: Philip Maltabar = Father's likeness. Adelaide denies.

**Ch XVI – "It Was My Father."** Kate sees photo; concludes father killed Stephen.

**Ch XVII – A Conference or Two.** Deville walks Kate home; father ill; father says Adelaide and Kate have "a secret"; Kate threatens to leave for Dresden.

**Ch XVIII – Friends.** Kate jealous of Olive; Deville and Kate reconcile.

**Ch XIX – A Corner of the Curtain.** Adelaide tells Kate a story: she (Adelaide) and Father (Horace Ffolliot, then "Philip Maltabar") were lovers; she refused marriage (free-love ideals); bore Kate; "You, are my child—and his!"

**Ch XX – I Am the Victim.** Kate rejects her; Olive and Deville arrive. Olive: "I'm sure I love him..." Olive wants Deville to propose (she to pay mortgages).

**Ch XXI – Out of Danger.** Father gone to London, then sea; Kate tells Adelaide: Deville is Adelaide's father's executor's son; Olive (ch.) . Deville brings violets; proposes? (ch XXV: Deville proposes; Kate lies she doesn't love him, under Olive's bribe offer of £10,000.)

**Ch XXII – An Unholy Compact.** Olive offers Kate: keep away from Deville; Olive will forgo vengeance against "Philip Maltabar."

**Ch XXIII – In the Plantation.** Kate avoids Deville; Adelaide offers Kate secretary post (£60/yr); Kate says she'll go to London. Deville catches Kate; "I wish I'd let that carriage go to the bottom."

**Ch XXIV – My Dilemma.** Kate accepts Adelaide's secretary post. Olive threatens Kate; "I hate you."

**Ch XXV – A Proposal.** Deville proposes; Kate refuses, lying ("I do not care for you").

**Ch XXVI – The Evidence of Circumstances.** Adelaide mentions Deville's conduct; Adelaide says she heard Deville threaten Stephen; they plan London.

**Ch XXVII – A Ghost in Whitechapel.** Kate sees father's likeness in Whitechapel (Commercial Road); Olive denies; Deville telegram.

**Ch XXVIII – Eastminster.** Father back, now Canon at Eastminster; Kate & Deville reconcile; he proposes; Kate accepts; Olive appears threatening.

**Ch XXIX – The Breaking of the Storm.** Father preaches; Olive recognizes him; father confesses killing Stephen in struggle ("blow for blow"); Olive vows to tell police.

**Ch XXX – The Master of Colville Hall.** Father's letter: he leaves Eastminster for London; Olive going to police; Kate follows father; Olive shadows; father found at "Colville Hall" (East End mission hall) preaching farewell to working-class listeners; he dies. Olive's detective mistakes a man; Olive: "I forgive. Farewell." Father: "This is happiness." END.

---

## BOOK 2: EMMANUEL APPADOCCA; OR, BLIGHTED LIFE. A TALE OF THE BOUCANEERS (Maxwell Philip, 1854, London: Charles J. Skeet). Two volumes; Vol. I chapters I–XV; Vol. II chapters XVI–XXXI. Dedicated to Harry Daniels; preface about slave-children in America; setting principally Trinidad.

Epigraph: Euripides, Greek.

**Vol I**
- **Ch I**: Gulf of Paria, March. Master of fishing-boat (mulatto, Spanish-extraction) with two blacks: Jack Jimmy (comic, 4½ ft, big eyes, bony jaw, "Garamighty!", "massa"). Indian canoe with 12 men (disguised, bearded, rifles) captures them. Stern man = Lorenzo (red cap, pirate officer). Master's knife knocked away by paddle; Jack Jimmy dives, is recaptured.
- **Ch II**: Black Schooner (balahoo, Death's head-and-crossbones device, red caps). Sebastian sentinel/officer. Captain (Emmanuel Appadocca) is ~25, mixed (quadroon-like), aquiline, Moorish crimson jacket, reading Bacon's *Novum Organum*, Aristotle. Lorenzo reports ships in harbour; the "Letitia" of Bristol (sugar, sailing for Bristol). Captain sends men to watch.
- **Ch III**: Feast; sailors' stories (Jim Splice, old Englishman, Llononois tale). Jack Jimmy blanketed; burned toe.
- **Ch IV**: Attack on the Letitia (Bristol ship, captain killed). Captive: aged priest, young lady Agnes (beautiful, Spanish colonial), Willmington (man who calls captain son; cabin musket). Captain recognizes Willmington as his father.
- **Ch V**: Lots/dividing booty; sailors ransomed; Jack Jimmy's loyalty.
- **Ch VI**: Duel over Francis's share; false friend killed; cannon-ball execution (drops overboard).
- **Ch VII**: Captain tries Willmington (father who abandoned son); sentence: cask adrift.
- **Ch VIII**: Willmington tied on cask ("machine"), set adrift; the schooner sails away.
- **Ch IX**: Lorenzo leaves letter for Agnes ("Lady, though I am a pirate…") pushed under door.
- **Ch X**: Agnes's reaction; priest and Agnes set in cutter to Trinidad; Jack Jimmy refuses to leave captain.
- **Ch XI**: Schooner at St. Thomas (Danish port). Captain sells cargo; Willmington rescued by British man-of-war (commander's son Charles Hamilton, Appadocca's friend from Paris university); Willmington accuses captain. Captain confesses.
- **Ch XII**: Appadocca's backstory: mother's death; left penniless; London; father's letter (Trinidad planter Willmington); woman on bridge (Thames); telescope lost; ship to Jamaica; San Domingo boucaniers.
- **Ch XIII**: Philosophy debate; Charles offers escape; Appadocca refuses.
- **Ch XIV**: Jack Jimmy escapes by canoe; rejoins schooner. Lorenzo plans rescue.
- **Ch XV**: Rescue attempt on man-of-war (drill through deadlight; shark interrupts); fails.

**Vol II**
- **Ch XVI**: Cutter voyage; master fisherman fights mutineers; reaches Trinidad; Agnes reunited with father at plantation.
- **Ch XVII**: Chase of Black Schooner by man-of-war (disguised as Mexican brig, brigantine signals "Au revoir"); schooner disguised as wreck "Sting"; midshipman kidnapped by Lorenzo.
- **Ch XVIII**: Midshipman tortured (spikes-box); reveals captain's safety.
- **Ch XIX**: Commander orders captain to be treated; signals by four flags deliberately; captain escapes by jumping overboard with a clay pitcher near the Dragon's Mouth.
- **Ch XX**: Swims, pitcher dissolves; reaches Venezuelan coast; rocks; Llaneros rescue him; Ranchero; Feliciana (Venezuelan daughter, in love). Fever.
- **Ch XXI–XXII**: Feliciana's plea (renounce piracy; "I shall follow you"); Appadocca leaves; kills a jaguar; fallucha rescue; Lorenzo recovers him.
- **Ch XXIII** (two chapters numbered XXIII): Captain's observation device (mirrors); Feliciana, in Guiria, meets horsemen; traveling; Appadocca's schooner; Willmington (rescued by Charles) jumps? (Note: Appadocca's supposed suicide reported to Charles.)
- **Ch XXIV**: Charles confronts Willmington ("bring your son to me"); Appadocca reported drowned; Willmington lands in Port-of-Spain, home on St. Ann's Road.
- **Ch XXV**: Appadocca (alive) confronts Willmington in villa; challenges Charles (Willmington's son) to duel; wins; villa looted; Willmington carried off.
- **Ch XXVI**: Feliciana and her guide consult the sorceress Mother Celeste ("Seek your lover amidst the tombstones").
- **Ch XXVII**: Appadocca at mother's grave (cemetery, Port-of-Spain); Feliciana finds him; he leaves; soldiers fire.
- **Ch XXVIII**: Mrs. Willmington finds Jack Jimmy and servants bound; Willmington's son goes after; man-of-war sails.
- **Ch XXIX**: Appadocca writes letter to Charles ("N.B. Recollect... tempest"); schooner pursued into Gulf; hurricane wrecks schooner on Trinidad rocks; Willmington drowns in torture-room; Appadocca and Lorenzo and Jack Jimmy survive.
- **Ch XXX**: Appadocca's farewell; leaps into sea; Jack Jimmy buries him beneath the solitary fig-tree; Feliciana arrives, goes mad over grave.
- **Ch XXXI**: Lorenzo marries Agnes (plantation of Carmonte-descended old cavalier); Jack Jimmy serves; Feliciana becomes the "Succouring Mother" in Venezuela, visits Trinidad yearly to tend the sea-grape tree over Appadocca's grave. END.

## BOOK 3: THE GREAT WHITE ARMY (Max Pemberton, Cassell, 1916)
Narrator: Surgeon-Major Janil de Constant (Vélites of Imperial Guard; formerly professor at Paris University; fled Revolution 1792; lived Leipsic). Nephew: Captain Léon de Courcelles (Vélites; handsome, womanizer; white horse; servant Gascogne). Sergeant Bourgogne (Vélites), Sergeant Bardot ("the antelope", Fusiliers; Gustav Bardot), Major Pavart (chasseurs), Captain Payard (dragoons), Sergeant Picard. Valerie St. Antoine (French-born, raised by Prince Nicholas's household in Moscow; her brother René; father Colonel St. Antoine, Chasseurs of the Line, dies at Slawkowo). Prince Nicholas (Russian assassin, Boris's son; loses arm to guillotine). Prince Boris (Moscow house). Joan d'Izambert (child, ~14), Gabriel d'Izambert (pontonnier, dies at Bérézina), old General d'Izambert.

**Ch I – The Woman on the Stairs.** Entry to Moscow 14 Sept 1812. Dandy lackey Heriot (servant of Prince Boris) takes Janil to house; dead artist youth (from Fréjus) shot in back; lackey killed by Janil's hand (throat). Valerie appears in a candle-lit gallery; hidden in Boris's chapel; then cupola gallery; Léon waves to her; Russians fire; chapel burned; Valerie rescued by Nicholas; Janil's "execution" by Russian soldiers; Léon rescues him; Janil and Léon watch burning palace ("A welcome to Moscow!").

**Ch II – The Guillotine.** Plundering of Moscow; Valerie's letter invites Léon to dinner; Janil goes with Sergeant Bardot in droshky to the house on a wooded island/moat (Ivan's Tower); Nicholas's mock-guillotine; Léon nearly beheaded; Bardot shoots bell; Léon rescued by French hussars; Valerie fetched the hussars. Léon: "I am still looking for her."

**Ch III – The Treasure in the Woods.** Retreat begins 19 Oct. Léon and Janil find woman Zayde (Zoida) with treasure of wrecked coach (murdered Prince Karasin). Taken to monastery (Russian, gold dome); monks drug them; Léon and Janil return; monastery empty; Cossacks flee after false bivouac fires. Treasure of Prince Karasin.

**Ch IV – Phantom Music.** Snow from 29 Oct. Valerie found in wrecked carriage with Baroness de Nivois and granddaughter (both dead). Slawkowo town; church of organ; drunken French soldiers; friendly-fire massacre at church; Colonel St. Antoine (Valerie's father) dies; Valerie burns her papers (Kutusoff plans); Janil sent to fetch her for Napoleon; she vanishes; "His Majesty left at one o'clock with a woman."

**Ch V – The Camp by the River.** Captain Payard (dragoons; blue eyes) takes Janil and Léon to Madame Pauline (Frenchwoman, wife of Russian officer; red-haired, green Cossack uniform) at Vitzala; Colonel Ferdinand Tcharnhoff returns; he shoots Payard; Pauline stabs Tcharnhoff; Janil and Léon escape; wolves; rescued by Red Hussars; Pauline seen later in Paris (Rue de Rivoli, June 1813).

**Ch VI – The Witch in Ermine.** Napoleon visits Madame Zchekofsky's house at Liadoui with her daughter Kyra (prophetess, sleepwalking); Janil impersonates Napoleon in cloak and hat; Cossacks drunk; Red Hussars rescue; Napoleon escaped to Wilna. Janil wakes drunk.

**Ch VII – Little Petrovka.** Near Krasnoë, Napoleon walks with Guard; Petrovka (girl disguised as hussar, Druobona) guides Léon and Janil and 150 men to farmhouse of moujik Serges; barn fire set by farmer's daughter Anna; Petrovka accused of firing barn; tried by officers Duhesne, Legard, Fournier; Léon defends her; Cossacks arrive; Petrovka saved (Cossacks are her friends).

**Ch VIII – The Affair at the Post-House.** Bérézina approach; lost in forest; three Cossacks; Léon kills their leader; Janil wounded in arm; wounded chasseur (of Châlons) dies; Janil and Léon disguised as Cossacks, reach post-house at Bobr?; Valerie there (Napoleon "tired of her"); fight with Cossack troop; Valerie reads Kutusoff aide's papers (ford/bridge held by Russians); Ney sends Léon with dispatch; Jewish couple Isidore and wife guide them into ravine (robbers, Orlof); they reach Bobr; Valerie rides in.

**Ch IX – We Cross the Bérézina.** Borisoff; Joan d'Izambert fetches Janil to brother Gabriel d'Izambert (pontonnier, fever); Gabriel reveals ford below Studianka; Valerie stays with d'Izambert family; bridging; night fall; Janil, Valerie, Joan cross by horse; Gabriel blows up bridge (ordered); presumed to die; Janil sees Gabriel in river.

**Ch X – The Last Review.** Retreat past Kovno; Bardot (sergeant) dies at Niemen-side farmhouse; Polish widow and sons attack; old merry Polish count (lancers from Orcha) captures Janil, Léon, Valerie, Joan; they go to Elbing (prison tower). Valerie, now "mistress" at prefect's house in Elbing (prefect Herrn Immo von Gustorf fled); French army arrives; "last review" by Marshal Ney; 22,000 survivors.

---

**END OF NOTES.** Use these notes for detailed questions about all three books.
